failures.evidence:
Surefire (WriteRateLimitTest.txt, run 2026-08-11T11:14-11:20 local = journal seq 162-165): 'Tests run: 5, Failures: 0, Errors: 5'. Every one is the same error, not an assertion: java.lang.IllegalStateException: Failed to load ApplicationContext ... Caused by: BeanCreationException 'entityManagerFactory' -> dependency 'flywayInitializer' -> 'Unable to obtain connection from database: FATAL: sorry, too many clients already / SQL State: 53300' (23 occurrences of that string in TEST-...WriteRateLimitTest.xml). No test method body was ever entered; even theApplicationContextLoads, which asserts only POSTGRES.isRunning() && REDIS.isRunning(), errored. Suite-wide: 276 tests, 0 failures, 5 errors, and this is the only class with a non-zero error count (grep over all 37 surefire .txt files); coverage_floor passed at 87.8% and routes_match_openapi passed 10/10, so the production surface is behaving.

Cause is the harness's connection budget, and it is arithmetic the implementation cannot influence. src/test/java declares 11 distinct @SpringBootTest property sets (base AbstractIntegrationTest plus AbuseReportRateLimitTest, AbuseReportReporterAgeTest, AnonymousCreateRateLimitTest, AnonymousLinkExpiryTest, ClickRateLimitTest, ConfiguredDefaultExpiryTest, SessionExpiryTest, SignInRateLimitTest, SignUpRateLimitTest, WriteRateLimitTest). AbstractIntegrationTest:80-84 states the design: 'Each distinct property set gets its own cached application context; the containers are shared across all of them.' Spring caches those contexts for the whole JVM (surefire is default single-fork, service/pom.xml has no forkCount/reuseForks config and is unchanged since scaffold e85ef36), so every one keeps a live HikariCP pool. There is no src/test/resources at all (directory absent) and no spring.datasource.hikari.* anywhere in src/main/resources/application.yml, so each pool takes Hikari's default maximumPoolSize=10; TestInfrastructure.java:44-47 starts a plain PostgreSQLContainer('postgres:17-alpine') with no withCommand, i.e. server default max_connections=100. By surefire report mtimes the base context plus 9 override contexts had already loaded before WriteRateLimitTest (11:20) — 10 pools x 10 = the whole budget — and WriteRateLimitTest's is the 11th context, which is exactly where Flyway is refused.

The implementation is structurally incapable of causing this: total connections are bounded by the sum of per-context pool maxima, and no main-code path opens a connection outside the pool (grep for getConnection/DataSource/HikariDataSource over src/main/** returns only ClickFlushJob's @Scheduled annotation). The implement diff under triage (f419f62) touches AbuseReportController, AbuseReportService and AppProperties only — no datasource, pool, migration or transaction-boundary change.

The contract does not promise anything that is being violated here: test-contract.json's harness section sanctions the per-class override mechanism ('Fixtures.SIGN_UP_LIMIT_KEY and Fixtures.ANONYMOUS_CREATE_LIMIT_KEY are driven down per class with @SpringBootTest(properties = ...)') and is silent on pool sizing (0 hits for pool/hikari/max_connections/context across the whole artifact). This is the 'mechanism is broken' case: the suite drives more application contexts than the container it shares can serve.

The repair is open to author-tests and needs no frozen file to move: TestInfrastructure.java is not in test-contract.json contract_files, and gates.py:_contract_frozen skips drift-checking any path the node owns ('if ctx.policy.check_write(rel).verdict is not PathVerdict.DENIED: continue'), while sdlc.yaml:292 gives author-tests write_paths service/src/test/**. Raising the container's max_connections (withCommand on the PostgreSQLContainer) or capping spring.datasource.hikari.maximum-pool-size in a test-scoped property source fixes capacity without touching a single assertion. implement cannot do either: sdlc.yaml:266 denies it service/src/test/**, and application.yml is a protected path whose own header says a node changing how the service connects to its database gets a human.

Marginal-cause note: AbuseReportReporterAgeTest, added by the most recent author-tests commit 4c9d74b, is the newest distinct property set and therefore the context that pushed the total over the budget — consistent with the previous verify (148 tests, 21 classes) never hitting this.

summary: One class failed: WriteRateLimitTest, 5 errors, 0 assertion failures anywhere in the 276-test suite. Nothing was asserted and lost — all 5 died before any test body ran, in Spring context startup, with Flyway unable to get a connection: "FATAL: sorry, too many clients already" (SQLState 53300). Fault is the test harness. The suite declares 11 distinct @SpringBootTest property sets, Spring caches one application context per set for the JVM's lifetime, each context holds a HikariCP pool at the default maximumPoolSize=10 (no src/test/resources exists and no hikari settings anywhere), and TestInfrastructure starts postgres:17-alpine with no withCommand, so max_connections is the default 100. Ten contexts had loaded before this class; its context is the eleventh. The prior triage's RedirectTest defect is gone (0 failures), so that repair landed; this is a new, purely mechanical ceiling. The implementation cannot be the cause: total connections are the sum of per-context pool maxima regardless of what the code does with them, no main-code path opens a connection outside the pool, and the implement diff under triage (f419f62) touches only AbuseReportController, AbuseReportService and AppProperties. Route to author-tests: TestInfrastructure.java is not a frozen contract file and contract_frozen skips files the node owns, so raising the container's max_connections or capping the per-context pool size is available there and weakens no assertion; implement is denied src/test/** and application.yml is a protected path. If I am wrong, the two things to check are (a) whether a human considers this a contract gap rather than a test defect — test-contract.json mandates the new per-class property overrides (SIGN_UP_LIMIT_KEY, ANONYMOUS_CREATE_LIMIT_KEY, MIN_REPORTER_AGE_KEY) that added the contexts, and says nothing at all about a connection budget, so the freeze arguably prescribed a suite that cannot fit; and (b) whether the CI host's Docker imposes a lower effective limit than the container's own default, which would make this environmental rather than either artifact's fault — worth confirming by re-running with max_connections raised before spending an attempt.
